cis_text.title: Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy

ai_guidance.llm: The service provider management policy must enforce a “conservative default” posture by mandating a safe baseline: disabling history retention, opting out of model training, pinning specific model versions, and disabling risky capabilities (e.g., agents) until validated. Policies must also require evidence of tenant isolation, logging clarity, and AI-specific incident notification SLAs. Permissive SaaS defaults may expose sensitive data for training or introduce risks via unmanaged feature updates and code execution. Enforcing these requirements, alongside data residency checks and vendor diversification, ensures that SaaS inference does not compromise data sovereignty, regulatory compliance, or operational resilience.
ai_guidance.agent: Ensure third-party providers receive access to only required data needed to perform authorized tasks. Prevent agents from sending sensitive or regulated data to providers that lack the necessary protections or authorizations.
ai_guidance.mcp: Define requirements including code signing, vulnerability disclosure processes, secure authorization behavior (PKCE where applicable, audience binding, scope minimization), accurate capability declarations, signed artifacts, vulnerability disclosure processes, and defined patch SLAs. Describe vetting procedures, approval processes, deployment restrictions, monitoring requirements, and incident coordination.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
